cards.text: The battle in the forest of Ephraim is over, and David's men have beaten the forces of his son Absalom, who rose up against him (2 Samuel 15:10; 18:6-7). Before it began, David told his commanders to treat Absalom gently (2 Samuel 18:5). Now Ahimaaz son of Zadok asks Joab, commander of David's army (2 Samuel 8:16), to let him run and tell the king the good news.

cards.question: Joab tells Ahimaaz he can carry good news another day, just not today. Why not today?

cards.text: So Joab turns to a Cushite and says, "Go, tell the king what you have seen." The Cushite bows and takes off running, and Ahimaaz is left standing there like the guy who volunteered for the big presentation and watched the boss hand it to somebody else.

cards.question: Ahimaaz takes the hint, lets the Cushite go and drops the whole idea.

cards.text: Ahimaaz won't let it go: no matter what, please let me run behind the Cushite too! Joab calls him "My son" and asks why he'd want to run when there's no reward waiting for him.

cards.question: Joab just told Ahimaaz there's no reward for running. What does Ahimaaz say back?

answers.text: He wants to run no matter what
He'll go if Joab pays him

cards.text: Joab finally gives in: "Then run!" Ahimaaz takes off by way of the plain, and friend, NOBODY in history has ever been this excited to do cardio.

cards.question: The Cushite left first. Ahimaaz goes by way of the plain, and he ___ the Cushite.

cards.text: Meanwhile, David is sitting between the two gates. A watchman goes up to the roof of the gateway, looks out and spots a man running alone.

cards.question: The watchman calls out to the king. What does David say a man running alone means?
Then the watchman spots a second man running alone, and David says this one brings good news too.

cards.text: The watchman says the first man looks like he's running like Ahimaaz son of Zadok. You know you've known a man a long time when you can pick out his jog from a rooftop.

cards.question: David hears the first runner may be Ahimaaz and calls him a good man who comes with good news.

cards.text: Ahimaaz calls out, "All is well!" and bows facedown before the king. Then he says, "Blessed be the LORD your God! He has delivered up the men who raised their hands against my lord the king."

cards.question: David just heard his men won the battle. What does he ask Ahimaaz?
Joab told Ahimaaz that the king's son is dead. Now Ahimaaz tells David exactly that.

cards.text: Ahimaaz says he saw a great tumult when Joab sent the runners, but he doesn't know what it was. Friend, the man RAN all that way, BEAT the other runner, and showed up with "I don't know."
David tells him, "Move aside," and "stand here." So Ahimaaz steps aside, and the king waits.
Just then the Cushite arrives and says, "May my lord the king hear the good news: Today the LORD has avenged you of all who rose up against you!"

cards.question: David asks the Cushite a different question than the one he asked Ahimaaz.

cards.text: Same question: "Is the young man Absalom all right?" The Cushite answers, "May the enemies of my lord the king and all who rise up against you to harm you be like that young man."

cards.question: The Cushite wishes David's enemies would be like that young man. What is he telling David about Absalom?
The king is shaken. David has been sitting at the city gate. Where does he go to weep?

cards.text: As he walks, he cries out, "O my son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom!" Right now he's not a king who just won a battle, friend. He's a dad.

cards.question: Then David says he wishes he had ___ instead of his son.

cards.text: Word reaches Joab that the king is weeping over Absalom.

cards.question: When the people hear the king is grieving over his son, that day's victory is turned into ___ for all of them.

cards.text: So the people slip back into the city quietly, as people steal away in humiliation after fleeing a battle. Friend, they WON, and they're creeping in like somebody late for work tiptoeing past the boss's office.

cards.question: While his army slips back into the city, David covers his face and cries out at the top of his voice.

cards.text: He cries, "O my son Absalom! O Absalom, my son, my son!" Then Joab goes into the house and tells the king that today he has disgraced all his servants, the ones who saved his life and the lives of his family.

cards.question: Joab tells David he has it all backwards. What does Joab say David does?

answers.text: Trusts those who lie to him

cards.text: Joab is NOT an ease-into-it kind of guy. He says he knows today that if Absalom were alive and all of them were dead, it would have pleased David.

cards.question: Joab still isn't done with David. What does he tell the king to do now?

answers.text: Go out and comfort his servants
Stay inside until the mourning ends
Go out and bury Absalom himself

cards.question: Joab swears by the LORD that if David doesn't go out, half his men will leave him tonight.

cards.text: Not half. Not a man will remain with him tonight, Joab says, and that will be worse than all the adversity David has faced from his youth until now. So the king gets up and sits in the gate.

cards.question: The word goes out, "Behold, the king is sitting in the gate." And all the people come before the king.

cards.text: Meanwhile, the Israelites on Absalom's side had fled, each man to his home. Keep your apron on, friend. There's more of this story still in the oven.

findings.problem: The story card has 3 sentences: the cry quote, "Right now he's not a king who just won a battle, friend." and "He's a dad." Only the opening card can go past 2 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
